_ext: keys below are pipeline extensions, additive to SPEC section 4

deliverables.text: Symmetry check: reflect right-half markers across the Y-axis (50-yard line), confirm they land on left-half partners.
The Expand worked in full: dilate all markers by the stated scale factor, find travel distances and required step size, then reverse-engineer the scale factor from one marker's start/end coordinates.
The Mirror Turn worked in full: rotate all markers 90 degrees about center, find travel distances and required step size; reason about the other rotation direction using D1's symmetry result.
Congruent-or-similar classification of each option's resulting formation vs. the original Block, justified by the transformation's defining property.
The ruled-out pivot: find all marker positions under a 180-degree rotation about center; explain the non-geometric rejection reason.
The verdict: compare Option A's required step size against both real ceilings, state headroom as a percentage, recommend.

balance.argument_a: The dramatic full-field visual is achievable: 27.05 in/step at 16 counts, over the comfortable 22.5 in/step standard but with real headroom under the 30 in/step aggressive ceiling.
balance.argument_b: Every marker's travel stays small (11.25 in/step) by the geometry of rotating about the formation's own center -- the safe, always-achievable choice, at the cost of visual impact.
balance.margin_basis: Option A's required step size (in/step) as a percentage headroom under the real 30 in/step ceiling, computed in cases/company-front/sensitivity_model.py from Appendix B/C/D figures.
balance.stability: Deliberately thin and NOT stable under a +/-50% flex of MA1 (scale_factor) or MA2 (counts) -- Tier 2 probe 5 shows the verdict flips under several flex directions (e.g. counts -50% or scale_factor +50%). This is the case's own pedagogical point, not an oversight: the Twist demonstrates exactly this fragility with a real, disclosed 2-count cut (16->14) that pushes Option A over the real ceiling. See FACILITATOR.md's Data Deep Dive and Twist sections, both of which state the margin is thin BEFORE the twist drops. Recorded as a disclosed, accepted P5 finding in QA_REPORT.md, not a redesign trigger -- same precedent as Cold Chain's own mechanical probe FAIL on a real, disclosed sensitivity (ROADMAP.md).

derived._note: Computed by cases/company-front/sensitivity_model.py. case-readiness should re-derive independently.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No public drill chart exists for this fictional show; set so the resulting step size sits between the real 22.5in/step comfort standard and the real 30in/step aggressive ceiling -- a genuine, realistic design choice.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing. Flexed +/-50% in Tier 2 probe 5: at -50% (2.2x) Option A drops to 9.55 in/step (very safe); at +50% (6.6x) Option A rises to 44.55 in/step (far exceeds the ceiling).

modeling_assumptions.basis: A round, common phrase-length in 4/4 drill writing (two 8-counts). Not derived from a specific real show's music.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Directly load-bearing -- flexed in the Twist (cut to 14 counts pushes Option A to 30.91 in/step, over the ceiling).
